subject: Mixed (Real Weightage)
description: 100 questions following the real PGP-CET 2025 subject weightage. Mix: 0 easy / 36 medium / 64 hard. Tier is relative: the hard third of the 60 papers by average question difficulty. Every question cites its source.

questions.question: A physiotherapist treating a child with Down syndrome should be cautious about:

options.D: Atlantoaxial instability when performing neck movements and sports

questions.explanation: Screen before activities such as gymnastics or trampolining.

questions.question: Patient circuits in therapeutic equipment are isolated from the mains by:
questions.explanation: Isolation reduces the risk of a shock path through the patient to earth.

questions.question: What is the general relationship between the intensity (load) of resistance exercise and the number of repetitions/sets possible?

options.A: There is no relationship — repetitions are independent of load
options.B: An inverse relationship: higher intensity/load permits fewer repetitions and sets, and lower load permits more
options.C: A direct relationship: higher load always allows more repetitions
options.D: Repetitions only depend on the patient's age, never on the load used

questions.explanation: There is an inverse relationship between exercise intensity (load) and the number of repetitions/sets possible — the higher the load, the fewer repetitions and sets that can be performed, and vice versa.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: The ‘safe position’ (intrinsic-plus) for immobilising the hand is:

options.C: MCP joints flexed 60–90° with IP joints extended and wrist in slight extension

questions.explanation: Prevents contractures of collateral ligaments.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Brukner & Khan, Clinical Sports Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Scapular dyskinesis in subacromial impingement most commonly involves:

options.B: Reduced upward rotation and posterior tilt, with weak lower trapezius and serratus anterior

questions.explanation: Rehabilitation emphasises scapular control.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Brukner & Khan, Clinical Sports Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Training to improve muscular (local) endurance typically involves:

options.A: A very heavy load for only 1-2 repetitions
options.B: Many repetitions (e.g. 3-5 sets of 40-50 reps) against a low, submaximal load
options.C: A single maximal isometric contraction held for 1 second
options.D: Complete rest with no muscular activity

questions.explanation: Muscle endurance training involves performing many repetitions against a submaximal load — for example, as many as three to five sets of 40 to 50 repetitions against a low resistance — and can be safely initiated early in rehabilitation since the load involved is low.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 6: Resistance Exercise — To Improve Muscle Endurance
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Carcinosarcoma is an example of a mixed tumour because it combines:

options.A: Two different carcinomas of the same epithelial origin
options.B: A malignant tumour of epithelium (carcinoma) with a malignant tumour of mesenchymal tissue (sarcoma) in the same lesion
options.C: A benign and a malignant tumour of the same tissue type
options.D: Tissue from all three germ cell layers

questions.explanation: Carcinosarcoma is the rare combination of a malignant epithelial tumour (carcinoma) and a malignant mesenchymal tumour (sarcoma) occurring together in the same lesion, such as in the thyroid.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) is most associated with:
questions.explanation: Pain peaks at 24–72 hours after eccentric loading due to micro-damage of connective tissue and muscle fibres.

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Paradoxical (see-saw) abdominal movement during inspiration suggests:

options.D: Diaphragmatic paralysis or severe respiratory muscle fatigue

questions.explanation: The abdomen moves inward on inspiration when the diaphragm fails; commonly seen in tetraplegia and GBS.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The anterior fibres of the deltoid mainly produce:
questions.explanation: Middle fibres abduct; posterior fibres extend and laterally rotate.

questions.question: Type I (slow oxidative) muscle fibres are characterised by:

options.C: High myoglobin, many mitochondria and resistance to fatigue

questions.question: Which is a component of Fried's frailty phenotype?

options.D: Unintentional weight loss, exhaustion, low physical activity, slow gait and weak grip

questions.question: Manual hyperinflation (bagging) in ventilated patients is used to:

options.A: Re-expand collapsed lung and mobilise secretions

questions.question: A p-value < 0.05 in a hypothesis test indicates that:

options.A: The null hypothesis is certainly true
options.C: The result is statistically significant at the 5% level (probability of a chance finding under H0 is < 5%)

questions.question: The ankle–brachial pressure index (ABPI) below which compression bandaging is contraindicated is about:

questions.question: The grid (point-by-point) method of laser application is used for:

questions.question: Which of the following is a recognised cause of thrombocytopenia (decreased platelet count)?

options.C: Administration of epinephrine causing splenic contraction

questions.explanation: Hypersplenism (an overactive spleen) is a cause of thrombocytopenia, along with bone marrow depression, certain viral infections (e.g. dengue, which particularly attacks platelets), and drug hypersensitivity. By contrast, splenectomy, epinephrine-induced splenic contraction, and trauma/surgery are causes of thrombocytosis (increased platelet count) — the opposite direction.
questions.sourceBook: AK Jain, Physiology
questions.sourceChapter: Platelets or Thrombocytes — Count and Variations
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Marked lateral rotation of a transfemoral prosthesis at heel strike may be caused by:

options.C: Excessive toe-out alignment, inadequate suspension or weak medial rotators
options.D: A prosthesis that is too long only

questions.explanation: Check alignment and socket fit.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Brukner & Khan, Clinical Sports Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The capsular pattern of the talocrural (ankle) joint is:

options.A: Plantar flexion limited more than dorsiflexion
options.D: Dorsiflexion limited more than plantar flexion

questions.explanation: Subtalar joint: increasing varus (limited inversion eversion pattern).
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A fall on the outstretched hand causing tenderness in the anatomical snuff box most classically suggests a fracture of which carpal bone?
questions.explanation: Scaphoid fracture is common after a fall on the outstretched hand and classically presents with tenderness and swelling in the anatomical snuff box, plus pain on longitudinal percussion of the thumb and index finger.
questions.sourceBook: BD Chaurasia's Human Anatomy — Upper Limb
questions.sourceChapter: Bones of the Upper Limb — Carpal Bones, Clinical Anatomy
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Compared with standing, the intradiscal pressure when sitting upright without support is:
questions.explanation: Lying supine produces the lowest disc pressure.

questions.question: Kienböck's disease is avascular necrosis of the:
questions.explanation: Preiser's disease affects the scaphoid.

questions.question: The physiological relaxation of the pelvic joints (symphysis pubis and sacroiliac joints) during pregnancy is primarily attributed to which hormones?
questions.explanation: Relaxation of the pelvic joints during pregnancy — increased width and mobility of the symphysis pubis, and similar changes in the sacroiliac joints — is attributed to the hormones progesterone and relaxin, facilitating the anteroposterior diameter increase needed during labor.
questions.sourceBook: Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics
questions.sourceChapter: Fetal Skull and Maternal Pelvis — Physiological Enlargement of Pelvis
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: The electromotive force (EMF) of a cell is:

options.C: The potential drop across the load
options.D: The potential difference across the terminals when no current is drawn

questions.explanation: Terminal potential difference falls below the EMF when current flows because of internal resistance.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Painless progressive jaundice with a palpable gallbladder (Courvoisier's law) suggests:

options.B: Carcinoma of the head of the pancreas
options.D: Gallstones in the common bile duct

questions.explanation: Courvoisier's law: if the gallbladder is palpable in the presence of jaundice, the cause is unlikely to be gallstones.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)

questions.question: In assessing whether an adverse event is caused by a drug, 'dechallenge' refers to:

options.A: Giving the drug for the first time to a new patient
options.B: Observing whether the adverse event subsides when the drug is stopped
options.C: Increasing the dose to see if the reaction worsens
options.D: A statistical technique unrelated to individual patient observation

questions.explanation: Dechallenge is observing whether the adverse event subsides when the suspected drug is withdrawn — a positive dechallenge (event resolves on stopping the drug) supports a causal relationship, alongside rechallenge (event reappears if the drug is restarted), though rechallenge is often unethical or dangerous to perform deliberately.
questions.sourceBook: KD Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: A positive hornblower's sign indicates a tear of the:
questions.explanation: The patient cannot externally rotate the arm at 90° abduction.

questions.question: A key reason K+ efflux is not fully compensated by Na+ influx at rest (helping maintain the resting membrane potential) is that:

options.A: The resting membrane is much less permeable to Na+ than to K+
options.B: There is no Na+ present in the extracellular fluid at rest
options.C: K+ cannot actually cross the membrane at rest
options.D: Na+ and K+ have identical permeabilities at rest

questions.explanation: Because the resting membrane is much less permeable to Na+ than to K+, the modest inward leak of Na+ does not offset the outward diffusion of K+ down its concentration gradient — contributing to the net negative charge that develops inside the cell at rest.
questions.sourceBook: AK Jain, Physiology
questions.sourceChapter: The Membrane Potentials — Genesis of Resting Membrane Potential
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: PLP-dependent decarboxylation of glutamate produces which inhibitory neurotransmitter?
questions.explanation: Glutamate undergoes PLP-dependent decarboxylation to form GABA (gamma-amino butyric acid), which inhibits nerve impulse transmission and is therefore classified as an inhibitory neurotransmitter — distinct from serotonin (from tryptophan) and histamine (from histidine), which are also PLP-dependent decarboxylation products but are not GABA.
questions.sourceBook: Satyanarayana, Biochemistry
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: When an apparent outbreak of infection is investigated and 'typing' shows the causal organisms do NOT share identical phenotypic/genotypic characteristics, the event is instead termed a:
questions.explanation: Confirmation of a genuine infectious disease outbreak usually requires typing evidence that the causal organisms share identical phenotypic and/or genotypic characteristics. If this is not the case, the apparent cluster is termed a pseudo-outbreak rather than a true outbreak.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Epidemiology of Infection — Outbreaks of Infection

questions.question: Unlike necrosis, apoptosis is characteristically NOT accompanied by:

options.C: Cell membrane changes of any kind
options.D: Any regulation by the cell itself

questions.explanation: Apoptosis is a controlled, internally programmed form of cell death ('cell suicide') that, unlike necrosis, occurs without triggering inflammation or collateral tissue damage — this is one of the key distinguishing features between the two forms of cell death.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology

questions.question: To achieve full passive range of hip flexion, the knee must also be allowed to flex. Why?

options.C: It is required purely to stabilize the pelvis

questions.explanation: The hamstrings cross both the hip and knee. Keeping the knee extended while flexing the hip stretches the hamstrings and limits how far the hip can flex; flexing the knee releases that tension, allowing full hip flexion range to be reached.
